::: {#exm-racket-postfix}
#### A postfix calculator in Racket

The method of @exm-postfix-stack uses a list as the stack (@def-stack):
`cons` pushes, and `first` and `rest` pop.
With `apply-op` from @exm-racket-evaluate,

```racket
(define (postfix-loop symbols stack)
  (cond [(empty? symbols) (first stack)]
        [(number? (first symbols))
         (postfix-loop (rest symbols) (cons (first symbols) stack))]
        [else
         (postfix-loop (rest symbols)
                       (cons (apply-op (first symbols)
                                       (second stack)
                                       (first stack))
                             (rest (rest stack))))]))

(define (evaluate-postfix symbols)
  (postfix-loop symbols empty))
```

In the last clause, `(first stack)` is the number $b$ popped first and `(second stack)` is the number $a$ under it.
`(evaluate-postfix '(7 2 - 3 4 2 * + *))` returns 55.

:::
